Commentary of al-Baghawi (*Ma'alim al-Tanzil*) on Surah 13, verse 39:

﴿Allah erases what He wills and establishes [what He wills]﴾. Ibn Kathir, Abu 'Amr, 'Asim and Ya'qub read "وَيُثْبِتُ" (*wa-yuthbitu*, "and He establishes") with the light form (*takhfif*, without doubling of the ث). The rest read it with the doubled form (*tashdid*). They differed over the meaning of the verse.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Qatadah said: Allah erases from the laws (*shara'i'*) and obligations (*fara'id*) what He wills, abrogating (*naskh*, the cancellation of a ruling by a later one) and replacing it, and He establishes what He wills of them, so He does not abrogate it.[[Recorded by al-Tabari: 16/39-40.]]

Ibn 'Abbas said: Allah erases what He wills and establishes, except for provision (*rizq*), the term of life (*ajal*), happiness (*sa'adah*) and misery (*shaqawah*).[[See: Tafsir al-Tabari: 16/485-486; for the other opinions on the interpretation of the verse, see the following pages of it. See also: al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/659-665.]]

We have also narrated from Hudhayfah ibn Usayd, from the Prophet ﷺ: "The angel enters upon the drop (*nutfah*) after it has settled in the womb for forty, or forty-five, nights, and says: 'O Lord, is it wretched or happy?' And both are written down. Then he says: 'O Lord, is it male or female?' And both are written down. Its deeds, its traces, its term of life and its provision are written, and then the scrolls are rolled up, and nothing is added to them or subtracted from them."[[Recorded by Muslim in *al-Qadar*, chapter on the creation of the human being in its mother's womb, no. 2644: 4/2037.]]

It is also reported from 'Umar and Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with them both, that they said: He erases happiness and misery as well, and He erases provision and the term of life, and He establishes what He wills.

It is reported from 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, that he used to circumambulate the House (the Ka'bah) weeping and saying: "O Allah, if You have written me among the people of happiness, then keep me established in it; and if You have written misery upon me, then erase me, and establish me among the people of happiness and forgiveness, for You erase what You will and establish, and with You is the Mother of the Book." The same is reported from Ibn Mas'ud.

In some reports: a man may have thirty years of his life remaining, but he severs his ties of kinship, so it is reduced to three days; and another man may have three days of his life remaining, but he joins his ties of kinship, so it is extended to thirty years.

Abu al-Wahid al-Maliḥi informed us, Abu Mansur al-Sam'ani informed us, Abu Ja'far al-Rayyani narrated to us, Humayd ibn Zanjawayh narrated to us, 'Abdullah ibn Salih narrated to us, al-Layth ibn Sa'd narrated to me, Ziyadah ibn Muhammad al-Ansari narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, from Fadalah ibn 'Ubayd, from Abu al-Darda', may Allah be pleased with him, that he said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, descends in the last three hours that remain of the night. In the first of these hours He looks into the Mother of the Book, which no one else looks into, and He erases what He wills and establishes."[[Recorded by al-Tabari in his *Tafsir*: 16/489, and in its chain is Ziyadah ibn Muhammad al-Ansari, who is "munkar al-hadith" (one whose narrations are rejected).

Al-Haythami said in *al-Majma'* (10/154-155): "al-Tabarani narrated it in *al-Kabir* and *al-Awsat*, and al-Bazzar narrated it in similar form, and in its chain is Ziyadah ibn Muhammad al-Ansari, who is munkar al-hadith."]]

It was also said: the meaning of the verse is that the guardian angels (*al-hafazah*, the angels who record human deeds) write down all the deeds and words of the children of Adam. Then Allah erases from the register of the guardian angels whatever has neither reward nor punishment, such as his saying, "I ate, I drank, I entered, I left," and similar speech that is true in itself, and He establishes what has reward and punishment. This is the view of al-Dahhak and al-Kalbi.

Al-Kalbi said: He records all speech, and then, when Thursday comes, He discards from it everything that has neither reward nor punishment.

'Atiyyah, from Ibn 'Abbas, said: This refers to the man who acts in obedience to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, then returns to disobedience to Allah and dies in misguidance; he is the one who is erased. And the one who is established is the man who acts in obedience to Allah and dies while in obedience to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic; he is the one who is established.

Al-Hasan said: ﴿Allah erases what He wills﴾, that is, whoever's term has come, He takes away; and He establishes whoever's term has not come until his term.

From Sa'id ibn Jubayr, he said: ﴿Allah erases what He wills﴾ of the sins of the servants, so He forgives them; and He establishes what He wills, so He does not forgive them.

'Ikrimah said: ﴿Allah erases what He wills﴾ of sins through repentance, and establishes good deeds in place of sins, as Allah, Exalted is He, said: ﴿Those, Allah will replace their evil deeds with good deeds﴾ [al-Furqan: 70]. As for al-Suddi: ﴿Allah erases what He wills﴾ refers to the moon, and ﴿and establishes﴾ refers to the sun, its explanation being His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿So We erased the sign of the night and made the sign of the day to be seeing﴾ [al-Isra': 12].

Al-Rabi' said: This concerns the souls, which Allah takes at sleep. Whoever He wills to die, He erases and withholds; and whoever He wills to remain alive, He establishes and returns to its owner. Its explanation is His saying, Mighty and Majestic: ﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death﴾ [al-Zumar: 42], and so on.

﴿And with Him is the Mother of the Book﴾, that is, the origin of the Book, which is the Preserved Tablet (*al-Lawh al-Mahfuz*), which is not changed or altered.

'Ikrimah said, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both: They are two books: a book other than the Mother of the Book, from which He erases what He wills and establishes; and the Mother of the Book, from which nothing is changed.

From 'Ata', from Ibn 'Abbas, he said: Indeed, Allah has a Preserved Tablet, five hundred years' journey in length, made of white pearl, with two covers of ruby. Each day, Allah has three hundred and sixty glances at it. ﴿Allah erases what He wills and establishes, and with Him is the Mother of the Book﴾. Ibn 'Abbas asked Ka'b about the Mother of the Book, and he said: It is the knowledge of Allah, what He is creating and what His creation will do.[[Al-Tabari preferred, from these opinions, the saying of al-Hasan and Mujahid, because Allah, may His remembrance be exalted, threatened the polytheists who asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for signs with punishment and warned them of it, and said to them: "It is not for a messenger to bring a sign except by the permission of Allah; for every term there is a decree" (al-Ra'd: 38). He informs them by this that His judgment concerning them has a fixed term recorded in a Book, and they will be delayed until the arrival of that term. Then He said to them: When that term comes, Allah will bring about whatever He wills among those whose term has drawn near and whose provision has ended, or whose destruction or humbling from exaltation or loss of wealth has come, and He will decree that among His creation. That is His erasing. And He establishes whatever He wills among those whose term, provision and sustenance remain, so He leaves them as they are and does not erase them. And with this meaning a report has come from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Then he cited the hadith of Abu al-Darda' already mentioned above. See: Tafsir al-Tabari: (16/488-489).]]

Commentary of al-Baghawi (Ma'alim al-Tanzil) on surah 13, verses 40–41:

﴿And whether We show you part of what We promise them,﴾ of the punishment, ﴿before your death, or We cause you to die﴾ before that, ﴿then upon you is only the delivery [of the message]﴾ — nothing is upon you except that, ﴿and upon Us is the reckoning﴾ — the recompense on the Day of Resurrection.

His saying, the Exalted, ﴿Have they not seen﴾ — meaning the people of Makkah, who ask Muhammad ﷺ for signs — ﴿that We come to the land, reducing it from its outskirts?﴾ Most of the exegetes hold that what is meant by this is the conquest of the lands of polytheism (shirk), for whatever is added to the lands of Islam is a loss from the lands of polytheism. The meaning is: ﴿Have they not seen that We come to the land, reducing it from its outskirts?﴾ — so We open it for Muhammad, land after land, around their land. Will they not then take heed? This is the saying of Ibn ʿAbbas, Qatadah and a group [of scholars]. [[See: al-Tabari: 16/493–494.]]

Others said: it refers to the ruin of the land. The meaning is: Have they not seen that We come to the land and lay it waste and destroy its people? Do they not then fear that We will do that to them? [[al-Tabari: 16/494.]]

Mujahid said: it is the ruin of the land and the taking of its people [in death]. [[See: al-Tabari 16/495.]]

And from ʿIkrimah, he said: the taking of people [in death]. And from al-Shaʿbi, the same.

ʿAtaʾ and a group said: its reduction is the death of the scholars and the passing away of the jurists. [[Tafsir al-Tabari: 16/497; al-Durr al-Manthur: 4/665–666; and al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak: 2/350 narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas regarding the meaning of the verse, he said: the passing of its scholars and its jurists and its best people.]]

Abd al-Wahid ibn Ahmad al-Maliḥi informed us, saying: Ahmad ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Nuʿaymi informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Yusuf informed us, saying: Muhammad ibn Ismaʿil narrated to us, saying: Ismaʿil ibn Abi Uways narrated to us, saying: Malik narrated to me, from Hisham ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, from ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿAmr ibn al-ʿAs (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Indeed, Allah does not seize knowledge by snatching it from the servants, but He seizes knowledge by seizing the scholars, until when He leaves no scholar, people take ignorant leaders; they are asked and they give verdicts without knowledge, so they go astray and lead others astray." [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in al-ʿIlm, chapter "How knowledge is seized": 1/194; and Muslim in al-ʿIlm, chapter "The lifting and seizing of knowledge," no. (2673): 4/2058; and the author in Sharh al-Sunnah: 1/4.]]

Al-Hasan said: ʿAbd Allah ibn Masʿud said: The death of a scholar is a breach in Islam that nothing can close as long as the night and the day alternate. [[Narrated by Ibn ʿAbd al-Barr in Jami ʿBayan al-ʿIlm, p. (240), from al-Hasan.]]

Ibn Masʿud (may Allah be pleased with him) also said: Hold fast to knowledge before it is seized, and its seizure is the passing away of its people. [[Narrated by ʿAbd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf: 10/252; al-Tabarani in al-Kabir: 9/189; al-Darimi in the Muqaddimah of his Sunan: 1/54; al-Khatib al-Baghdadi in al-Faqih wa al-Mutafaqqih: 1/43; and al-Bayhaqi in al-Madkhal ila al-Sunan, p. (272), and he said: this is mursal, but it has been narrated in a connected chain through the Syrians. See the note of Dr. Muhammad al-Aʿzami in the same place.]]

ʿAli (may Allah be pleased with him) said: The likeness of jurists is only like the palms: when a palm is cut off, it does not return.

Sulayman said: People will remain in good as long as the first generation remains, until the later one learns; but when the first dies before the later one has learned, the people perish.

It was said to Saʿid ibn Jubayr: What is the sign of the people's ruin? He said: The ruin of their scholars. [[al-Tabari said in his tafsir (16/497–498): "The most correct interpretation of that is the saying of the one who said: 'Have they not seen that We come to the land, reducing it from its outskirts?' — referring to the victory of the Muslims, the companions of Muhammad ﷺ, over it, and their subduing its people. Will they not take heed from that, so that they fear their (the Muslims') dominance over their land and their subjugation of them? This is because Allah threatened those among the polytheists of his people who asked His Messenger for signs with His saying: 'And whether We show you part of what We promise them, or We cause you to die, then upon you is only the delivery, and upon Us is the reckoning.' ﴿And Allah judges; there is no repeller of His judgment,﴾ no one who turns back His decree and no one who annuls His ruling, ﴿and He is swift in reckoning.﴾

Will they not take heed from that, so that they fear their (the Muslims') dominance over their land and their subjugation of them? This is because Allah threatened those among the polytheists of his people who asked His Messenger for signs with His saying: 'And whether We show you part of what We promise them, or We cause you to die, then upon you is only the delivery, and upon Us is the reckoning.' Then He, may His remembrance be exalted, rebuked them for their poor consideration of what they witnessed of Allah's action against their fellow disbelievers, while they still asked for signs. So He said: 'Have they not seen that We come to the land, reducing it from its outskirts?' — by subduing its people and prevailing over it from its edges and sides, and they do not take heed from what they see of that."]]

﴿And Allah judges; there is no repeller of His judgment,﴾ no one who turns back His decree and no one who annuls His ruling, ﴿and He is swift in reckoning.﴾

Commentary of al-Baghawi (*Ma'alim al-Tanzil*) on Surah 13, verses 42–43:

﴿And those before them had already plotted.﴾ That is, those before the idolaters of Makkah. *Al-makr* (scheming, plotting) is bringing harm to a person from a direction he does not perceive.

﴿To Allah belongs all plotting.﴾ That is, with Allah is the requital for their plotting. It has also been said: Allah is the Creator of all their plotting. The good and the evil are in His hand, and benefit and harm come from Him, so no one's plotting harms anyone except by His permission.

﴿He knows what every soul earns, and the disbelievers will know for whom is the final reward of the abode.﴾ The people of the Hijaz (*Ahl al-Hijaz*) and Abu 'Amr read *al-kafir* (singular), and the others read *al-kuffar* (plural).

﴿For whom is the final reward of the abode.﴾ That is, the end result of the Hereafter, when they enter the Fire and the believers enter Paradise.

﴿And those who disbelieve say, "You are not a messenger." Say, "Sufficient is Allah as witness between me and you."﴾ [He is a witness that] I am His messenger to you. ﴿And [so is] whoever has knowledge of the Book.﴾ He means: the believers among the People of the Book (*Ahl al-Kitab*) also bear witness to that.
